title: Search cumulative thresholds for probabilistic fanouts of at least 64
question: Can the same categorical draw select high-fanout groups faster using the existing admitted weights?
summary: A 512-group near-uniform fixture saves 70–361 ms across three verified pairs. The 64-group pairs save 13–21 ms. The early-heavy control is nearly even and the two-group control adds about 8 ms at the medians.

workloads: 64 and 512 near-uniform groups, 512 groups with 90% first, and a two-group 80/20 control.

validation.summary: Exact seeded internal lookup agreement including zero weights and threshold boundaries. Hosted export verifies conservation, configured order, subsequences, zeros, CSV caps and marker.

limitations: Three complete paired repetitions per cell with uncontrolled warm cache. One high-fanout pair is slow in both arms. Isolated lookup probe excludes hashing and job work.
exclusions: Cross-Run membership parity with fresh entropy, native elapsed time and physical disk I/O.
